answer: Work-history credit stops sybils: influence comes only from tasks attested by at least three non-kin peer witnesses, and every exercise of power - vote or audit - irreversibly consumes credit, like cutting a yarrow stem. Each spend leaves a plume: a public trail verifiers check against one-time nullifiers, so two clones cannot spend the same history twice. An attacker building N fake histories pays N×T task cycles while gaining at most one history's credit, and all records settle in the basalt ledger, which rejects duplicated histories. Cloning dilutes influence; it never multiplies it.
